source.title: Defending Against Malicious Finetuning by Scaling Train-time Adversarial Attacks
source.authors: Hao-Min Wen; Shi Chen; Qing-Yu Shi; Si-Yuan Liu; Min-Rui Luo; Jingzhao Zhang; Tian-Xing He

page_placements.theme: Replay, data selection and constraints can preserve downstream safety

record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-completion rates after malicious fine-tuning and prompt-based jailbreak attacks, but does not reproduce the cited studies’ first-token KL or compliant-prefill measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports post-attack ASR, which directly measures harmful compliance after malicious fine-tuning or prompt-based jailbreak attacks. It does not report a before-attack ASR for these comparisons. Theoretical gradient-error bounds and loss curves are not direct measurements of the claim versions. To stay within the 60-row limit, the Table 1 rows cover every listed method, attack dataset, and benchmark; Table 2 rows omit LAT, and other reported results are summarized under rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper (PATCHER). It reports post-attack harmful-compliance rates for baseline safety-aligned models in a new setting: base models given Alpaca instruction tuning, then safety alignment, then full-parameter fine-tuning on a mix of 200 harmful and 800 GSM8K samples. These results bear on V1. GCG suffix attacks on the aligned checkpoints bear on V4. Neither comparison reports a before-attack ASR. It is not T2, because it does not aim at the claim's question with another method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that existing alignment-stage defenses fall short against full-parameter fine-tuning. They admit PATCHER stays vulnerable at moderate or high learning rates, with some optimizers (RMSProp) and under DPO attacks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates a defense against full-parameter malicious fine-tuning and prompt-based jailbreaks; it does not reproduce the original small-data fine-tuning or first-token KL/prefill measurement recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported ASR changes across attack dataset, evaluation benchmark, defense method, and prompt-jailbreak method. The paper also describes sensitivity to attack budget, dataset size, optimizer, and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight-space adversarial training against reused many-step attack vectors (PATCHER) lowers post-fine-tuning ASR: to 18–27% on in-distribution attacks versus 39–59% for SFT. It stays high on Toxic-DPO attacks (57–71%), and at lr 5e-5, with RMSProp and under DPO attacks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment-stage defenses that simulate many-step full-parameter attacks partially resist harmful fine-tuning, with robustness depending on attack dataset, learning rate, optimizer and loss.

fits_no_version.finding: ICA few-shot and PAIR prompt jailbreaks reach high ASR on aligned checkpoints, e.g. ICA 95.5–100% on SFT, Vaccine and TAR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context and iterative prompt jailbreaks defeat refusal in small aligned models.

record.problems: No un-attacked ASR is given alongside the Table 1 post-attack results, limiting direct quantification of the increase caused by the attack. Main ASR results use a judge model; the paper reports human calibration with one undergraduate annotator and imperfect precision/recall. The prompt-jailbreak table reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 LAT results (three attack conditions) are omitted to keep within 60 rows. Also omitted: Table 7 results for Qwen3-4B and Llama3-8B; Table 9–13 adaptive attack and LoRA results; and other appendix evaluations. These report further ASR variation by model, training configuration, loss, data schedule, and fine-tuning strategy; the main table results and prompt-attack results were retained.

untested.parts: No sweep from few to hundreds of harmful examples in isolation. Harmful data is always mixed with benign GSM8K data, and there is no pre-attack ASR.
A benign-only case (poison ratio p=0, Figure 11) is plotted, but no values are given in the text. No other benign-only fine-tuning is reported.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models is not measured.
Prefilling and decoding changes are not tested; only GCG suffixes are. No no-attack ASR is given for the Table 2 checkpoints.
Parameter or rank localization of safety is not studied.
The causes of shallowness are not studied.
No training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens; PATCHER is a weight-space adversarial defense.

missing.what: LoRA harmful fine-tuning: SFT ASR 1.3%/67.5% (rank 32, lr 1e-5/5e-5) and 8.9%/73.9% (rank 128)
Optimizer, learning rate and batch size effects on SFT ASR: Muon 7.1, RMSProp 55.7, lr 5e-5 79.9, batch size 16 31.9
Alternative-judge ASR (SFT average 13.5–21.6%) and relaxed threshold of 4 (SFT average 63.8%)
Other models: SFT post-attack ASR for Qwen3-4B (56.2/39.7/67.2) and Llama3-8B (90.7/48.3/91.3)
Poison-ratio sweep including p=0 (benign-only), plus dataset-size and step sweeps; values are in figures only
Gradient-ascent, DPO and data-schedule attacks on SFT (e.g. Harmful-to-Benign 30.2, Benign-to-Harmful 44.5)

record.verdict_notes: The pre-attack ASR of aligned models is never reported, so V1 support assumes low baseline refusal failure. Attack data always mixes harmful with benign samples. Rows for PATCHER (the study's own method) and for the ICA/PAIR attacks are unlinked. The LAT row in Table 2 (GCG 47.0) was omitted by the reader. Tranche changed from T2 to T3.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments do not isolate fine-tuning on only harmful examples: the default test-time attack configuration includes harmful and benign data. The study does not test a sweep of few-to-hundreds of harmful examples in isolation.
No benign-only fine-tuning condition measures whether ordinary or carefully chosen benign data raises harmful compliance.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
The prompt attacks include GCG, ICA, and PAIR; no compliant-opening prefill or decoding-change condition is tested.
No parameter or rank localization of safety behavior is measured.
The paper proposes an explanation for PATCHER’s robustness, but does not test why safety behavior would be shallow.
PATCHER is a defense against malicious fine-tuning, but the study does not test whether safety training spreads behavior beyond early response tokens or whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.condition: Full-parameter fine-tuning of SFT-, Vaccine-, Booster- and TAR-aligned Qwen2.5-1.5B on 200 harmful plus 800 benign samples for 2000 steps, judged by Qwen3-Max (score 5)
relationships.reason: Post-attack ASR is 25–76% for SFT (T1–T9) and up to 91–97% for TAR (T28–T36). This rests on the inference that pre-attack ASR was low, which is not reported.
relationships.display_finding: Post-attack success was 25–76% for the SFT-aligned model and up to 91–97% for TAR. Pre-attack rates are not reported, so the rise is inferred.

source_check.condition: Full-parameter fine-tuning of SFT-, Vaccine-, Booster- and TAR-aligned Qwen2.5-1.5B on 200 harmful plus 800 benign samples for 2000 steps, judged by Qwen3-Max (score 5)
source_check.reason: Table 1 confirms substantial post-attack harmful compliance across these alignment methods. The authors explicitly report vulnerability to full-parameter fine-tuning; the increase from pre-attack compliance remains inferred because no pre-attack ASR is reported.

relationships.condition: LoRA harmful fine-tuning at lr 1e-5, or the Muon optimizer
relationships.reason: From the text, not rows (Tables 12 and 9): SFT-aligned model ASR stays 1.3% (rank 32) or 8.9% (rank 128) under LoRA, and 7.1% with Muon. At lr 5e-5 LoRA it rises to 67.5–73.9%. So erosion depends on optimizer and learning rate.
relationships.display_finding: The SFT-aligned model's ASR stayed at 1.3% (rank 32) or 8.9% (rank 128) under LoRA at lr 1e-5 and 7.1% with Muon, but rose to 67.5–73.9% under LoRA at lr 5e-5.
